description: Recovery from a kill after implementation and before testing, on build task g-article-filters (row G): killed at the first `go test` call, then resumed in a fresh process.
setup: test "$(go env CGO_ENABLED)" = 1 || { echo 'row G needs cgo for mattn/go-sqlite3: the image has no C compiler (gcc, libc6-dev)' >&2; exit 1; }
notes: Copy of build task g-article-filters (ticket, hidden tests, reference patch, setup). Kill point: the first stream line carrying a Bash tool call whose command runs `go test` (with or without a cd prefix or env assignments). The line is emitted before the command runs, so the arm is killed after writing code and before seeing any test result. Why it marks the phase for both arms: native normally runs go test once it has implemented the change; in Daedalus, step 1 (feature-plan, PLAN mode) runs no tests, and the first go test comes from the implementer subagent at the end of its implementation (or, failing that, from test-runner) inside step 2 [subagent tool calls must appear in the parent's stream-json; verify in T0]. Difference: an arm that runs a baseline `go test` before editing is killed before implementing anything; that run's diff is then empty at kill time, and killed_at plus the step stream show which call matched. Resume: one fresh process whose prompt points to the run's ticket file ({ticket_path}, the ticket delivered as data, as in the arms' own prompts), the interruption note, the arm's resume_hint and the shared instruction. Success = hidden tests pass at the end. Needs cgo in the image, like the build task. budget_usd is a placeholder; the harness reserves twice the cap. The hidden tests and the reference patch were type-checked offline with go vet against the cached modules; they have not been run.
